title: Range XOR Queries with Subarray Reversals
summary: Given an integer array nums and a series of queries, update the array by setting a value at a specific index, compute the bitwise XOR of a subarray, or reverse a subarray.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a series of queries, update the array by setting a value at a specific index, compute the bitwise XOR of a subarray, or reverse a subarray. For each range XOR query, record the result in the order the queries are given.
constraints: nums and queries each have up to 100,000 entries.
[1,index,value] updates one position; [2,left,right] reports inclusive range XOR; [3,left,right] reverses that range.
Updates and reversals persist, and XOR answers must follow query order.
hints: Range reversal changes order but not subtree membership or XOR, making an implicit balanced tree with a lazy reverse flag natural.
Store sequence position by subtree size, range XOR as an aggregate, and reversal as a child-swap flag.
Split around each range, read or toggle its middle tree, then merge the three pieces; isolate one node for updates.
Split/merge preserve sequence order, aggregates are refreshed locally, and lazy swaps exactly represent every pending reversal.
editorial: Split/merge preserve sequence order, aggregates are refreshed locally, and lazy swaps exactly represent every pending reversal.

tests.explanation: The first range XOR is five; after the update and reversal, the whole-array XOR is eight.
Updating the first value makes the full XOR two; the later reversal produces no additional answer.
